uses.loci: Bellinati printed77-78/PDF109-110 original page images; Leto printed87-88/PDF88-89 original page images, nn55/59; ISEP publisher card.
uses.finding: Bellinati explicitly describes Thursday Mass, consecrated bread and reservation at ordinal ff89v-92v, and Friday celebrant communion at ff92v-95r. The later post-prandium procession is separately attributed to C56f60 and is properly excluded. Leto cites E.57 edition127g before Easter Missa maior and 140e before Ascension solemn Mass. These are precise local rubrical loci, not a generic ritual-title inference.

uses.loci: Vildera printed p. 139 original first-page image, 153 source list; Leto printed p. 86; ISEP publisher card.
uses.finding: First-page image clearly names Anna Vildera. Her c. 1256–1275 E.57 c. 43v text concerns Christmas Matins; it is correctly not imported as Mass text. Leto gives 1234–1304; publisher gives thirteenth century. A 1201–1300 plotting coordinate is explicitly the selected publisher-century attestation, not first use or an independently dated period of implementation.

uses.loci: Preserved IRHT HTML fields64-85; Bellinati printed44 original image n22; Calendaria D.30 row; Toigo printed48/PDF86 original image and n153; Diocese2021 item13/PDF2.
uses.finding: IRHT1301-1310 conflicts with Bellinati post1323 and Calendaria c1338. Toigo says early-fourteenth-century Roman Missal, Padua provenance, Matthew c70r/v and Mark c74r/v, with a very short visible Matthew melody crop. Official item13 identifies f20v Epiphany introit. This supports a scoped chant witness but no full Missal contents, actual altar-use date or local recension. Null stage dates and removal of narrow candidate plotting dates are appropriate.

uses.finding: Pad16/57 combines B16* and E.57. Its high folio numbers247ff cannot be silently assigned to ordinal E.57. Packet rejection of this shortcut is appropriate, as are separate treatment of D.47 Gregorian transmission, Passau Pataviense and Leto MFR prayers.

sources.inspection: Complete 2014 Claudio Bellinati, Contributo alla storia della cattedrale di Padova nell'età di Giotto e della cappella Scrovegni, 201-page publisher-linked PDF acquired. Printed pp. 26–29, 43–45, 56, 74–79 inspected; pp. 44, 77–78 checked against page images. D.30 is post-1323 and associated with Cathedral Inventory 1350 f. 14v; E.57 Thursday Mass and reservation are described at ff. 89v–92v, Friday communion at ff. 92v–95r. The exact original E.57 leaves and archival inventories were not acquired. Publisher landing route https://www.padovaeilsuoterritorio.it/archivio/quaderni links this public download. At p. 43 the C.47/D.34–Cholet identification is tentative (sembra); p. 44 distinguishes the planned 1352 Holy Cross altar destination from its 1357 construction.

Whole Diego Toigo, Intonazioni monodiche della Passione in Italia fra i secoli XIII e XVI, doctoral dissertation, 228-page PDF acquired. Printed pp. 47–48 and manuscript crop on p. 48 checked against image. D.30 is expressly Missale Romanum, early fourteenth century, with Matthew Passion melody at c. 70r/v and Mark at c. 74r/v; B.31 is expressly Roman use for Padua Friars Minor (p. 47 n. 151). Crop does not constitute inspection of the complete original leaf or whole Mass formulary.

Entire two-page 21 December 2021 Diocese of Padua Ecce advenit list acquired and inspected. Item 13 names D.30 f. 20v, Epiphany introit Ecce advenit, fourteenth century, Padua. Item 4 identifies D.34 f. 17v as Paris 1281–1292 Franciscan Missal, Christmas major Mass. These are catalogue descriptions of identified leaves, not a direct reading of the original leaves or proof of a distinct Padua recension.

Complete public Calendaria HTML acquired. Padova Biblioteca Capitolare-Archivio D.30 row reports c. 1338, Padova Duomo. This disagrees with IRHT 616628's 1301–1310 copying range; neither value is silently substituted for the other. The calendar row is a specialist index, not inspected original calendar evidence.

Whole 150-page Inferno e Paradiso, first edition 2025 (not 2026 URL year), acquired. Francesca Leto chapter pp. 86–88 inspected and pp. 87–88 checked against images. Notes 55 and 59 cite E.57 edited sections 127g (Easter procession before Missa maior) and 140e (Ascension procession before solemn Mass). P. 86 reports wider date 1234–1304. The chapter's separate Franciscan Missal exemplar MFR is not E.57 and is not used to supply E.57 prayers.

Complete IRIS record acquired; abstract and file-availability section inspected. Author Antonio Lovato's abstract identifies the 2002 study as direct examination of E.57 and other named cathedral books, including chants prescribed for Mass and Office in local thirteenth–fifteenth-century processions. The record explicitly has no attached file. An abstract is not the full contribution or original manuscript collation.

Complete 17-page Anna Vildera, Formulari processionali per il canto del Vangelo Liber generationis, De musica disserenda IX/1–2 (2013), pp. 139–155, acquired. P. 139 and source list p. 153 identify E.57 c. 43v, dated c. 1256–1275. Its printed rubric concerns Christmas Matins and is not counted as a Mass proper or complete Eucharistic book.

versions.title: Padua Cathedral Liber ordinarius E.57: local Eucharistic rubrics
versions.date: Thirteenth-century manuscript; narrower c. 1256–1275 in Vildera 2013, wider 1234–1304 in Leto 2025
versions.source_locus: Bellinati 2014 pp. 26–29, 77–78: E.57 ff. 1r–7v, 89v–92v, 92v–95r; Leto 2025 pp. 87–88 nn. 55, 59: E.57 edited sections 127g, 140e.
versions.qualification: A cathedral order book with explicitly local Mass rubrics, not a complete Padua Missal or an independently collated recension. The primary manuscript and complete 2002 edition/facsimile remain unacquired. E.57's Christmas Matins rubric c. 43v and Leto's separate Franciscan exemplar MFR are not imported as E.57 Eucharistic text.

versions.title: Padua Cathedral B.26: Ildebrandino Conti's missal
versions.date: Attested in bequest 24 September 1352; copying date not established here
versions.source_locus: Bellinati 2014 p. 44 and n. 20: B.26, bequest 24 September 1352 for cathedral Holy Cross altar, Inventory 1350 f. 12v; cites Bernardinello 2007 I pp. 205–209.
versions.qualification: Identified physical missal and local ownership/destination. No copying date, complete contents, actual celebration or independent Padua recension is established by this bequest report. No dated stage proposed. Bellinati, p. 44, describes the 1352 destination as a Holy Cross altar then planned, actually built in 1357; the bequest does not establish celebration at that altar in 1352.

versions.title: Padua B.31: Roman Missal for the city's Friars Minor
versions.source_locus: Bellinati 2014 p. 44 n. 21: dated scribal colophon; Toigo dissertation p. 47 n. 151: Missale Romanum ad usum fratrum minorum civitatis Padue, Matthew Passion c. 80r and unnotated Mark space c. 85r.
versions.qualification: Roman use for Padua Friars Minor; Padua copying and custody do not establish a separate Padua diocesan Missal. Reported 1328 colophon has not been checked on the original page. No new local recension or stage proposed.

versions.title: Cholet Franciscan Missal: surviving Padua C.47 and D.34 volumes
versions.date: D.34 dated 1281–1292, Paris, by diocesan catalogue; linked volumes' detailed dating uncollated
versions.source_locus: Bellinati (2014), p. 43, cautiously proposes (sembra) that C.47/D.34 survive from the former three-volume Cholet missal; pp. 43–44, notes 15–17, give owner/donor context. Official diocesan Ecce advenit (2021), item 4, separately identifies D.34 f. 17v as a Paris 1281–1292 Franciscan Missal.
versions.qualification: Bellinati's identification of the two volumes with the Cholet missal is tentative. D.34's independently catalogued Paris 1281–1292 Franciscan identity and date do not automatically apply to C.47. Exact divisions, the missing third volume, original leaves, local reception and altar use remain uninspected; no complete Padua book or two recension states are established.

versions.title: Padua Cathedral D.30 Roman Missal and calendar
versions.date: Fourteenth century; IRHT 1301–1310 conflicts with Bellinati post-1323 and Calendaria c. 1338
versions.source_locus: IRHT 616628 preserved HTML lines 64–85; Bellinati 2014 p. 44 n. 22 (post-1323; Inventario 1350 f. 14v); Toigo dissertation pp. 47–48 n. 153 (D.30 Matthew c. 70r/v, Mark c. 74r/v, manuscript crop); Diocese Ecce advenit 2021 item 13 (Epiphany introit f. 20v); Calendaria D.30 row (c. 1338, Padova Duomo).
versions.qualification: Identified Roman Missal of Padua provenance, with named chant loci and a short original musical crop inspected. Full original Mass prayers, calendar, local rubrics, approval and actual altar use remain uninspected. Conflicting narrow copying dates remain unresolved; no independent Padua diocesan recension is asserted. B.31 is a separate Roman-Franciscan book; Pataviense may denote Passau.

semantics: Two source-described states, no complete Missal or transition. E.57 has bounded local Eucharistic rubrics; D.30 remains unpositioned with IRHT 1301–1310, Bellinati post-1323 and Calendaria c. 1338 unresolved. Anna Vildera (2013) is the correct attribution; E.57 Christmas Matins, separate MFR prayers, Pad16/57 combined chant loci and Passau Pataviense are not imported as Padua Mass text. Modern source bytes remain outside Git.
